utterances.text: I remember the talks with Mr. Vance, because I was with Mr. Milan Babic talking to Mr. Vance in Belgrade, and I know how they evolved. Mr. Cyrus-Vance told us that that was for the first time that the United Nations was using the so-called ink blot system. Obviously we Serbs seemed to be -- seemed to be guinea pigs, because things tend to happen for the first time to the Serbs or with the Serbs, and so has this Tribunal been set up as the first one precisely for the Serbs. But to go back to how the talks between Mr. Babic and Mr. Cyrus-Vance evolved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR MACURA
utterances.text: Mr. Vance proposed that the ink blots, namely the forces of the United Nations, should deploy in the Krajina territory and thus protect that zone. However, Mr. Babic insisted that the ink blot system should be applied to Croatian towns, because Serbs were perishing, suffering in Croatian towns. They were getting killed there. Mr. Babic's proposal was that the ink blots should be applied in Croatian towns and not on the territory of the SAO Krajina. However, Mr. Vance wouldn't hear of it. And then Mr. Babic gave another proposal, and it was that United Nations troops should be deployed along the line of separation and not in the depth of the SAO Krajina territory. Mr. Cyrus-Vance would not accept that either, and that is how those talks ended. Then Mr. Vance went to talk to Mr. Milosevic, to bring pressure to bear on him to have his plan accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I think that perhaps we have come to the end of this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How much longer are you going to be with this witness, Mr. Milovancevic? Because you have now taken four-fifths of the time that you originally estimated, which is actually not supposed to be valid because of the two decisions that have been handed down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, of course mindful of our second estimate, I will be finished tomorrow during the first session, by the end of the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, the second estimate is also invalid because of the second decision that was handed down. You've got to align yourself with the second decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have not been instructed by this second decision in terms of the duration of this witness' testimony. As far as I understood the situation, we have submitted our revised estimate of the duration of the testimony to the Bench, to the Trial Chamber, and of course we have to respect the decision brought on that basis. I have just tried to explain how we understand the situation. What we understood is that here Mr. Macura's testimony should last for ten hours. We have spent three hours and 45 minutes, and we have another hour and 15 minutes in the morning, which would be approximately half of our time. So it is one hour and 15 minutes for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, do you read decisions as they get handed down?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you read the last decision which said that you are supposed to have filed a revised filing by yesterday giving your revised estimates in accordance with the last decision, with that decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you file it yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I addressed you yesterday, as President of this Trial Chamber, saying that we have made the decision, reviewed the time needed for all witnesses, and we do not see any possibility for revising our time, apart from taking completely unjustified arbitrary steps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I understand you to be saying, therefore, you are not going to obey that order? Because it was an order to you in that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No. That's not what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, can I ask you to do me a favour? Go and read that document and let's talk about it tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll start tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of September, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24
